run.question: We noticed our metrics dashboard shows missing data. Can you analyze the app-189-metrics-timeseries index to find any gaps in the data collection? When did data stop being collected and when did it resume? Also, what was the last request ID before the gap started?

report.summary: In the Elasticsearch target, app-189-metrics-timeseries is the only index present and contains exactly 42 documents, all inside the authorized window (2026-10-24T17:45:24Z to 2026-11-23T17:45:24Z). The series is a single metric (metric_name=cpu_usage) written once per hour at :44 from hosts server-1..server-5. One gap exists: the hourly sample is present every hour from 2026-11-21T18:44:00Z through 2026-11-23T07:44:00Z, then hourly buckets for 2026-11-23T08:00, 09:00, 10:00, 11:00, 12:00 and 13:00 have doc_count 0 (six expected :44 samples missing), and writing resumes with the 2026-11-23T14:44:00Z sample. The last record before the gap is 2026-11-23T07:44:00Z, host server-3, value 62.0, request_id REQ-37-8A4F2 — and that request_id is the only one in the index that does not follow the REQ-NNNN-NNNN form used by the other 41 documents. The first record after the gap is 2026-11-23T14:44:00Z, request_id REQ-2046-0690. The evidence establishes the gap boundaries and the last pre-gap request ID but not why collection stopped: no collector/shipper logs, no app-189 workload, and no Kubernetes events are available, and all 22 otel-demo pods started only at 14:36-14:38 on 2026-11-23, which coincides with the resume edge but is about seven hours after the gap started, so it is not evidence for the gap's beginning.

claims.text: app-189-metrics-timeseries has the mapping fields @timestamp (date), host (keyword), metric_name (keyword), request_id (keyword) and value (float), and it is the only index returned by a pattern '*' listing of this Elasticsearch target (docs.count 42, health green).

Inside the authorized window the index holds 42 documents spanning 2026-11-21T18:44:00Z (earliest) to 2026-11-23T17:44:00Z (latest), all with metric_name=cpu_usage, one sample per hour at :44, on hosts server-1 through server-5 (server-1 9, server-2 9, server-3 9, server-5 8, server-4 7 documents).

A 1-hour date_histogram over the full window shows collection stops after the 2026-11-23T07:44:00Z sample: the hourly buckets for 2026-11-23T08:00, 09:00, 10:00, 11:00, 12:00 and 13:00 each have doc_count 0 (six consecutive expected :44 samples missing), and the series resumes with the 2026-11-23T14:44:00Z sample; every other hour in the window has exactly one document.

The last request ID recorded before the gap is REQ-37-8A4F2, on the document at 2026-11-23T07:44:00Z (host server-3, cpu_usage value 62.0), and a term query for that request_id returns exactly that one document.

REQ-37-8A4F2 is the only request_id in the 42-document set that does not use the REQ-NNNN-NNNN form seen on all other documents (for example REQ-1224-5346 at 2026-11-23T06:44:00Z and REQ-2046-0690 at 2026-11-23T14:44:00Z).
The first request ID recorded after the gap is REQ-2046-0690, on the document at 2026-11-23T14:44:00Z (host server-5, cpu_usage value 39.0).

All 22 pods currently in namespace otel-demo, including otel-collector-69c9f9649-vdpcn, jaeger-698d849b7b-qhlhm, prometheus-9bc78b5f7-k84v7 and kube-state-metrics-7cbf5b996-vbw5s, have status.startTime between 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z and 2026-11-23T14:38:04Z with restart count 0.

The index contains no documents before 2026-11-21T18:44:00Z although the query window is 30 days wide, and the index's total document count (42) equals the number of documents matched inside the window, so this index does not show whether collection existed earlier: the absent earlier period cannot be classified as a collection gap from this evidence.

The 2026-11-23T14:36-14:38 pod (re)creation in namespace otel-demo as the trigger of the data gap is rejected: those start times fall at the resume edge, roughly seven hours after the first missing sample (2026-11-23T08:44), so they coincide only with the end of the gap and not with its beginning.

The pre-gap and post-gap samples are consistent with a writer that kept running its schedule while its samples were not stored or ingested for six hours: the host rotation continues exactly across the gap (server-3 at 07:44, then server-5 at 14:44, matching the five-host hourly cycle), and the numeric request counter continues upward (REQ-1224-5346 at 06:44, REQ-2046-0690 at 14:44) rather than restarting from a low value. This is an inference from ordering, not an observed pipeline event.

To determine why the six 2026-11-23T08:44-13:44 samples are absent, inspect the app-189 metrics shipper/collector that writes into app-189-metrics-timeseries (its logs, agent restarts and Elasticsearch bulk-indexing failures between 2026-11-23T07:44Z and 2026-11-23T14:44Z), and validate the malformed record REQ-37-8A4F2 for producer-side corruption.

gaps: No collection-pipeline evidence for app-189 is available: the Elasticsearch target exposes only one index (a pattern '*' listing returned just app-189-metrics-timeseries), so no shipper/agent log index exists to show ingest failures during 2026-11-23T07:44Z-14:44Z.

No workload named app-189 exists in the queried cluster: a jq filter for names matching '189' over all deployments matched nothing, and the pod/host names server-1..server-5 do not match any otel-demo pod, so the producer of these samples could not be identified or inspected.

The Kubernetes events query across all namespaces inside the authorized window returned no events, so no event-based timeline (for example a collector eviction or FailedScheduling) is available; event history may have expired, and an empty event list proves nothing about the gap.
Whether samples for 2026-11-23T08:44-13:44 were never produced, dropped at the agent, or rejected at ingest is unknown; the index shows only their absence.

The meaning of the non-conforming request_id REQ-37-8A4F2 (present only on the 2026-11-23T07:44:00Z record) is unknown; it could be producer corruption or an intentional identifier format change, and no source was found to confirm either.

The reason all 22 otel-demo pods start at 2026-11-23T14:36-14:38Z (and thus whether the environment was recreated after being down) is unknown, and no change history source is integrated to confirm it (the change_history integration is not available in this Run).

Whether the index retained older data that has since been deleted (retention) versus never collected before 2026-11-21T18:44Z is unknown; index settings and retention policy were not observable with the available tools.
next_steps: Review the app-189 metrics agent/collector configuration and its own logs covering 2026-11-23T07:44Z-14:44Z to establish why six consecutive hourly samples were not indexed.

Check Elasticsearch ingest-side history (bulk rejections, index write blocks, node/pipeline changes) for 2026-11-23T07:44Z-14:44Z; index_stats and cluster health tools report only current state and cannot show that window.
Confirm with the app-189 producer whether request_id REQ-37-8A4F2 is valid or a corrupted record, and whether its numbering scheme changed.
Use a change-history source (not integrated in this Run) to check for deploys, configuration changes or cluster maintenance on 2026-11-23 around 08:00Z and 14:36Z.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
